_about: Hand-entered inputs for scripts/model/build.mjs. Two kinds: (1) public numbers read from a document that fetch.py does not parse, each with its source; (2) the model's own parameters, which are choices, not data. The paper labels both.

equityWeights._source: FTSE Global All Cap Index factsheet, data as at 30 October 2026, country breakdown. U.S. 62.89%. Emerging is my sum of the markets FTSE classifies as emerging (about 9.6%); developed ex U.S. is the remainder.

credit._source: Investment grade: expected loss is half the spread, the long-run finding of Giesecke, Longstaff, Schaefer and Strebulaev (2011). High yield: 3.61% weighted-average annual default rate, 1971-2013 (Altman and Kuehne 2014) times a 60% loss given default (40% recovery is the convention in CDS pricing and my assumption).

_materialityBp: An asset stays on the menu only if it adds at least this many basis points a year to a stand-alone investor's certainty-equivalent return, at some risk aversion on the grid.

savingsRate._source: Vanguard, How America Saves 2026: average total contribution rate (participant and employer) 12.1% in 2025.

incomeBeta._note: Share of human capital that behaves like stocks. Model parameters, bracketed by the literature the paper cites; not estimates.

estimationRisk._note: Not used in the base case. Kept for the sensitivity run only.

morningstar._source: Morningstar, 2026 Target-Date Fund Landscape (data as of Dec. 31, 2025): median equity exposure 45 years from retirement 93%; U.S. stocks 62% of the Morningstar Global Markets Index at end-2025.
